stem: Meera's school in Pune follows a solar calendar with 365 days each year, but every fourth year an extra day (29 February) is added. Why is this leap day needed?

options.text: The Moon takes extra days to orbit the Earth, so the calendar must be corrected.
The Earth takes about 365¼ days to revolve around the Sun, so the extra quarter-days must be collected to keep the calendar aligned with the seasons.
The extra day is added only as a festival holiday and has no scientific reason.
The Sun moves faster in some years, so the calendar must be made longer.

teacher.key_rationale: A solar year is about 365.25 days; the extra quarter-days accumulate to roughly one day every four years, so a leap day keeps the calendar synchronised with the seasons. A wrongly invokes the Moon, C treats leap years as arbitrary, D incorrectly claims the Sun's motion changes.
